source.title: Train Faster, Perform Better: Modular Adaptive Training in Over-Parameterized Models
source.authors: Yubin Shi; Yixuan Chen; Mingzhi Dong; Xiaochen Yang; Dong-Sheng Li; Yujiang Wang; Robert P. Dick; Qin Lv; Yingying Zhao; Fan Yang; T. Lu; Ning Gu; L. Shang

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures modular NTK eigenvalues and reports how their temporal changes relate to overfitting and validation loss, using a different measure from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports mNTK dynamics and generalization outcomes for its proposed MAT training method. The optimizer, architecture, batch-size and explicit-regularization comparisons in the claim versions are not tested. Cited results from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study investigates modular NTK eigenvalues and selective module updating, not any of V1–V8. Its eigenvalues are not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness (V7), and MAT is not an adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison (V4). Generalization results alone do not test the specified versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors associate mNTK principal eigenvalues with module trainability, argue that updating modules with small eigenvalues can impair generalization, and conclude that MAT reduces training computation while improving reported held-out performance. The noisy-feature explanation and its extension from two-layer theory to deep networks remain interpretive rather than directly demonstrated.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes selective modular backpropagation based on mNTK eigenvalues; it does not reproduce the original methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported validation/test outcomes vary by training method; MAT, random module selection, multirate updates, and vanilla training produce different values. The paper also uses different MAT thresholds across BERT, Switch-Transformer, and VGG settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation loss begins increasing around epoch 45 while training loss continues decreasing and examined layer-wise mNTK principal eigenvalues settle at low values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the examined BERT setting, low late-training mNTK principal eigenvalues coincide with overfitting; the proposed explanation involving noisy features is not causally established.

fits_no_version.finding: MAT reports lower converged test log perplexity than vanilla training for BERT (4.27 versus 4.41) and Switch-Transformer (1.68 versus 1.74), and slightly higher VGG16 accuracy (93.86% versus 93.77%), with reduced computation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective module updating based on mNTK eigenvalues can improve held-out performance and training efficiency in the tested workloads.

fits_no_version.finding: MAT reduces computation to convergence across five BERT scales, with reported savings increasing from 26.4% to 50.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MAT's relative computational savings increase across the tested BERT scales.

record.code_released: https://github.com not stated as a code release; referenced tool repositories are https://github.com/pnnl/torchntk and https://github.com/microsoft/DeepSpeed
record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, 2023)
record.problems: The mNTK-to-generalization account is partly theoretical and described as a possible explanation; the temporal-overfitting result is limited to one 4-layer BERT setting and is presented in figures with no uncertainty stated. Test metrics in the method comparisons do not provide training error or training–test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. The cited prior-work findings are not this study's results. Table 5 reports pruning comparisons, but these do not directly measure a version's named behavior or training–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance performance with random labels under matched architectures and recipes.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of learned or imposed local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that compensate for large batches.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The Hoffer citation supplies a weight-distance argument, not a test or operational use of V5's batch-size finding. Missing training–test gaps are decisive for V7, but are not a general reason to exclude results from versions defined by held-out performance; these method comparisons are excluded because their interventions do not match any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: 4-layer BERT
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training loss, validation loss, and layer-wise mNTK principal eigenvalues during masked modeling on half sequence length.

conditions.value: after epoch 45, described as overfitting stage

rows.measure: Training and validation loss; temporal change in principal mNTK eigenvalues
rows.baseline: During the first 45 epochs, validation loss had not begun increasing and the principal eigenvalues continually decreased.
rows.value: After the 45th epoch, validation loss increased while training loss continued decreasing; principal eigenvalues converged to excessively low values.
rows.note: The paper describes the eigenvalue changes as a possible explanation for overfitting, not as a causal test.
rows.check: The reported temporal association is supported but measures no listed version. Model identity is internally inconsistent: Figure 3 calls it a four-layer BERT, whereas Section 2.2 names layers 3, 6, 9 and 12. The stated 12 heads per layer is not established for this particular experiment.
